profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I am a software engineer at Google working on Google Drive.

I received two CS degrees from Colorado School of Mines: a BS in 2014 (with minors in mathematical sciences and economics), and a MS in 2015.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Drive (2018-present)
- Improved reliability and latency of several API request shapes. (Java)
- Added new file suggestion strategies for Drive Workspaces.
- Replaced internal investigation tools, increasing usability, auditability, and performance. (API design)
- Prototyped several file suggestion features with other teams. Notable launches include the suggested files card for Chrome's new tab page.
- Contributed new features to the models that power suggestions on Drive apps, ran A/B experiments to evaluate quality uplift. (TensorFlow)
- Integrated Gemini into Drive
- Responded to production emergencies as part of the team's on call rotation.

Apps Script (2016-2018)
- Built tools that enabled organization admins to manage Apps Scripts. Worked on the frontend (Google Closure, JS) and backend (Java)

positions.title: Adjunct Professor
positions.description: Taught one section of an introductory programming course (CSCI261) in C++ during fall semesters (2017, 2018, and 2019) and spring semesters (2021).

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
On-campus jobs included:
- Research assistant for the CS Unplugged program (SmartGeo Fellow recipient) Aug. 2014 - Dec. 2015
- Taught AP CS at Mullen High School, May 2014 - December 2014
- Maintained websites for Chemistry, Provost, and EECS professors, April 2012 - Aug. 2014
- Undergraduate Research Assistant for EECS doctoral candidate, Aug. 2013 - May 2014
- Graded for Computer Organization (CSCI341), Aug. 2013 - May 2014
- Taught AP CS at Golden High School, Aug. 2013 - May 2014
- Led after-school Java club for middle school students, Jan. 2013 - May 2013
- Tutored Calculus I & II, Aug. 2012 - December 2012
- Led after-school STEM group for elementary students, Aug. 2012 - Dec. 2012

positions.title: SWE Intern
positions.description:
I worked on the team that builds the internal knowledge management system that powers Google Help. My project was to create a backend monitoring tool to measure latency of pub/sub messages, detect when messages were erroneously dropped, and to log when messages were not sent because of a publishing error. I used Google infrastructure to build out an RPC service for production systems to notify, and was able to integrate and run my project in a dev environment by the end of the summer.

Buzzwords I learned/used:
Guava, Guice, Bigtable, Remote Procedure Call, Publish/Subscribe

positions.title: Web & Mobile Team Intern
positions.description:
- Created an API using existing internal tools to configure 3D geometry from a web browser
- Participated in agile meetings to estimate story points
- Presented final results to business, engineering, and knowledge teams

positions.title: Web & Mobile Team Intern
positions.description:
Designed and implemented an extension to export dynamic components. Components could then be viewed and edited in a web browser (without needing to have SketchUp installed).

More information on my summer project can be found in the blog post I wrote (see attached link for details). I also interacted with an agile team and met internal deadlines regarding my project. On top of that, I worked alongside other great engineers, and provided feedback through code reviews and weekly developer meetings.

positions.title: Office Associate
positions.description: Set up the platform for an online Driver Ed course, and worked in the front office (data entry, phone calls, customer service).

honors.title: Rising Star Award
honors.description: “Brandon is one of those students that only comes along every 5-10 years. Let me illustrate this point with a few examples. First, Brandon is a top student with the intelligence and character to excel in the most rigorous of undergraduate programs. Second, in less than one year, Brandon has become an extremely valuable member of my research team. Third, Brandon is a really nice kid. He is always considerate, exhibits a genuine concern for his colleagues, and goes out of his way to assist others. He also has an easy-going personality, a great sense of humor, and is an excellent communicator. Brandon's role as the SHPE Outreach Chair illustrates these facts. In this role, Brandon has been involved in several K-12 outreach activities, sharing his enthusiasm for computer science with kids. For example, he completely developed a project that was appropriate for middle school children (a project that involved building and programming a robotic car), and then deployed the project by working over a several week period with a local middle school technology teacher. Over 90 students (in four classes) at the middle school benefited from this project. He also helped me with a "Discovering Technology" program that I organized during Fall 2012, where four groups of 12 kids each (kids in 4th and 5th grade) came to Mines to learn about STEM fields. Brandon completely developed the content to teach these elementary school children about Kudo Game Lab (http://www.kodugamelab.com). After this session, several parents contacted me to share how their child enjoyed what they learned. One parent wrote "Kodu is a winner. My daughter came home and built a new world for 1.5 hours, so she obviously enjoyed it." In summary, in my 19 years of advising and mentoring undergraduate students, I have the experience to know that Brandon is one of those students that all advisers dream to teach/mentor. He's intelligent and an ideal team player.”
honors.issuer: Issued by Colorado School of Mines - Student Activities · May 2013

projects.title: Golden High School AP CS Club
projects.description: I set out to tutor local students in programming, only to find no courses offered to teach computer science! An effort to tutor evolved into an effort to teach. Not only are students learning fundamental computer science concepts, but I am ensuring the curriculum includes the AP topics so students can test for college credit. Three students took the test, with one achieving a 5, and another receiving a 4; both received college credit from the College Board.

publications.title: Assessing Computational Thinking in CS Unplugged Activities
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the 2017 ACM SIGCSE Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education · Mar 8, 2017

publications.title: Using student performance to assess CS unplugged activities in a classroom environment
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the 2016 ACM Conference on Innovation and Technology in Computer Science Education · Jul 11, 2016

organizations.name: Blue Key Honor Society
organizations.description: The National Blue Key Honor Society is a premier honor society that recognizes college students at senior institutions of higher education for balanced and all around excellence in scholarship leadership and service. The CSM chapter of the Blue Key was chartered in 1926 and is one of the longest serving chapters of the National organization. On the CSM campus we have a long history of service and and spirit to the campus and Golden Community. We are the caretakers of "Blaster the Burro" when he is on campus and caretakers of the M on Mt. Zion.

organizations.name: Kappa Mu Epsilon
organizations.description: Kappa Mu Epsilon (KME) is a specialized honor society in Mathematics. The national organization was founded in 1931 to promote the interest of mathematics among undergraduate students. KME chapters are located in colleges and universities of recognized standing which offer a strong degree program in mathematics. The chapters' members are selected from students of mathematics and other closely related fields who have maintained standards of scholarship, have professional merit, and have attained academic distinction.
